verdictStatement: Both of my v8 items and both of Codex's are repaired, and the capacityPause repair goes further than I asked: splitting lossOrCapacity into a temporary pause and a permanent quarantine was the ask, but inventing pendingTerminalizerRecord to catch a terminalizer that arrives mid-pause answers a case I only gestured at. carrierQuarantineRecord is now a properly assigned SC-OPS byte-set with sole writer, retention, backup, purge, migration, recovery and a gated clearing path — which closes the one place v8 relied on a durable fact it had not placed. Healthy TERMINAL now derives solely from the journal marker, exactly as Codex asked. The blocker is what those two new byte-sets brought with them. Both are SC-OPS. One states that it is not dropped to make room; the other does not, and its whole purpose depends on surviving until consumption. Neither is inside SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL, whose scope is stated twice as 'only for DR-105 grant-journal bytes'. So the design's own promise — that a terminalizer arriving during a pause is 'not swallowed' — rests on a durability property that is either unauthorized for one record or unstated for the other, depending on which reading of the SC-OPS bounded rule you take. This is the defect class that blocked v4 and v5, reappearing on the bytes v9 added rather than on the journal.

blockers.title: The two newly assigned SC-OPS byte-sets take inconsistent positions on the class's 'bounded' rule, and neither is inside the supersession — so the 'not swallowed' promise is not durably established
blockers.subjectQuote: carrierQuarantineRecord classRuleCarveOut: 'These bytes are a single current standing record per carrier, not a sequence journal. They are not dropped to make room.' pendingTerminalizerRecord classRuleCarveOut: 'Single current pending record per carrier. FIRST-wins: a second terminalizer does not replace the first. Secret VALUES are excluded.'

measurement.bothAreSCOPS: Both new entries carry class SC-OPS with standing ASSIGNED. The SC-OPS class rule carried verbatim from file 04 at /stateTextCarriedVerbatim/linesVerbatim is 'Journaled/redacted/bounded; backup/purge scope disclosed; never a peer evidence writer.'
measurement.neitherIsInsideTheSupersession: I checked the scope text twice over. of[3] displaces the boundedness rule 'as applied to DR-105 grant-journal bytes only'. whatIsSuperseded opens 'Three displacements only, and only for DR-105 grant-journal bytes'. Measured against the 'of' array: no entry names carrierQuarantineRecord or pendingTerminalizerRecord. Both records are moreover defined as external to the journal — 'stored outside that generation's grant journal', 'MUST NOT be a grant-journal append' — so they are expressly NOT grant-journal bytes and cannot fall inside a displacement scoped to them.
measurement.limbOneUnauthorizedDeparture: carrierQuarantineRecord asserts 'They are not dropped to make room' and 'Archival is copy, not truncation'. That is the same no-drop property the grant journal has, and for the journal this artifact correctly treats it as a departure from the SC-OPS boundedness rule requiring a named supersession displacement, owner concurrence and an overturn clause. For these bytes it is asserted with none of that.
measurement.limbTwoTheMissingProperty: pendingTerminalizerRecord does NOT claim no-drop. Its retention is 'Until consumed by the terminal-marker append, or until the generation is otherwise TERMINAL' — a bound that ends at consumption, with nothing requiring survival until then. Its writeRule handles write FAILURE ('Write failure keeps the pause and MUST NOT resume ordinary appends') but not loss after a successful write. capacityPause then states: 'When capacity returns: if pendingTerminalizerRecord is present, the ONLY lawful journal append is the grant-journal-terminal-marker … if ABSENT, ordinary appends resume on the same carrier.' So if the record is bounded away between write and consumption, the carrier silently resumes ordinary appends and the projectPurge or grantGenerationClosure that arrived during the pause is lost.
measurement.againstTheDesignsOwnPromise: terminalization.capacityPauseIsNotFailClosedNoAppend states 'A terminalizer that arrives during the pause is stored as pendingTerminalizerRecord, not swallowed.' Under the class rule as it applies to these unsuperseded bytes, exactly that swallowing is permitted.
measurement.robustUnderBothReadings: If the SC-OPS 'bounded' rule reaches single-record stores, limb one is an unauthorized class-rule departure and limb two is an open swallow. If it does not reach them, limb one is unnecessary and limb two is safe — but then the artifact's own drafting is inconsistent, because it thought a no-drop sentence was needed for one record and not the other, and neither reading is stated anywhere. On every reading the 'not swallowed' guarantee is asserted rather than established.

blockers.whyBlocker: This is the defect class that produced my blocker at v4 and my and Codex's blockers at v5: a departure from the SC-OPS journaled/redacted/bounded rule stated outside the scope of the named supersession. The artifact's own reviewGuidance still carries the attack line for it. It matters more here than as a drafting point because the pendingTerminalizerRecord limb is a live correctness hole in the very mechanism v9 introduced to close my v8 S-1: a purged or closed carrier can resume ordinary appends if one small record is dropped, which is the outcome FIRST-wins terminalization exists to prevent. And because these are the first SC-OPS byte-sets whose durability the design depends on outside the journal, the question of what authority licenses their no-drop property is not answerable from the artifact.
blockers.whatIsNotWrong: Placing these two records was the right move and is a genuine repair of my v8 S-2 and Codex's SCC-V8-B1 — I am not asking for them to be withdrawn, nor for either property to be weakened. The lifecycles attached to them are careful, the sole writer is correctly identified as the same broker with no second ordering authority, and routing both irreversible actions through the D-096 (A) gate is exactly right. The defect is authority and consistency, not design.
blockers.minimumRepair: Extend SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL's 'of' and whatIsSuperseded to cover the SC-OPS boundedness rule as applied to carrierQuarantineRecord and pendingTerminalizerRecord, and widen the 'only for DR-105 grant-journal bytes' qualifier accordingly — the owner set already listed covers these bytes, and standing's overturn clause needs the same one-line extension it received at v6. Then give pendingTerminalizerRecord the same explicit no-drop property carrierQuarantineRecord has, so 'not swallowed' is backed by a stated durability rule rather than by the absence of a contrary one. If instead the position is that the boundedness rule does not reach single-record standing stores at all, state that once at the SC-OPS class level and delete the now-unnecessary no-drop sentence from carrierQuarantineRecord.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed.attack: capacityPause and uncertainTailLoss are a relabelling of v8's single lossOrCapacity clause
attacksAttemptedAndFailed.result: FAILED. They are genuinely different states with different consequences: the pause keeps the same carrier and resumes ordinary appends when capacity returns; the quarantine is permanent, writes an external record, forbids promotion and forces continuation onto a new carrier. capacityPause is expressly excluded from failClosedNoAppend, and terminalization carries a dedicated clause saying so. This is the split I asked for at v8 S-1.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed.attack: carrierQuarantineRecord is a second marker class in disguise, or is written into the journal
attacksAttemptedAndFailed.result: FAILED. It is expressly external — 'stored outside that generation's grant journal', 'MUST NOT be written into the journal', 'MUST NOT be appended to that carrier's grant journal' — and failClosedNoAppend states healthy TERMINAL is never inferred from it. The v8 concern that the artifact declined to mint a second marker class while relying on an unplaced standing is resolved in the honest direction: the standing is placed as its own byte-set rather than smuggled into the journal.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed.attack: The three carrier standings now overlap or can be inferred from one another
attacksAttemptedAndFailed.result: FAILED. Each has a distinct named source: healthy TERMINAL solely from the journal terminal marker; uncertainTailLoss and witnessless-restore revocation from carrierQuarantineRecord; FROZEN-UNDER-OVERTURN from the applied coordinator overturn recording of the named supersession, via frozenUnderOverturnSource. failClosedNoAppend explicitly forbids inferring healthy TERMINAL from the others. I looked for a state reachable by two routes with different consequences and did not find one.

coordinatorNote: One blocker, and it arrived with the repair rather than instead of it. v9 did the right thing by placing the two durable facts the v8 design leaned on; what it did not do is ask what authority lets those new SC-OPS bytes escape the class's boundedness rule, which is the question this row has already answered twice for the journal itself. The repair is small and the owner set already listed covers it — extend the supersession's scope beyond 'grant-journal bytes only' to the two records, extend the overturn clause the same way, and give pendingTerminalizerRecord the no-drop property its own promise depends on. I would flag the second half as the part that matters operationally: as the bytes stand, a purged or closed carrier can resume ordinary appends if one small record is lost, which is exactly what FIRST-wins terminalization was built to prevent. S-1 is a one-line enumeration fix, and I would take the opportunity to make that sentence derive from bytePlacement rather than list byte-sets, since this is the third time it has had to be widened. I did not read the other current v9 reviewer, did not edit the subject or the prompt, did not edit file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, did not apply SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL, did not mint a D-096 (A) grant, did not mark any DR SATISFIED, and did not commit.
